featured_reviews.review_text:
Happy experience...
Thanks doctors....

Yes my friends,
People write many nasty experience they face in hospital or with doctors. Very few write their sweet experiences in hospital or with doctors.

So I thought to share my excellent sweet experience with a small, faraway hospital but with exceptional expertise in the field of knee replacement and other orthopedic and neurological complication.

My wife Operated for knee replacement on 15th...At 11 in the morning (to 2.30 pm) including recovery time inside operation theatre...

Then shifted to ICU.
Operation was good, my wife was in jolly mood and smiling while coming out from OT after the replacement ... But after 2 hrs of shifting to ICU, the real pain started... Wife was crying like mad for pain... But through medication by 8 pm it has started reducing... and she slept.
Nxt day, 16th, morning no pain...and shifted to pvt room cabin. I also staying in the same room with her. Excellent clean cosy room with all necessary requirements like AC, TV, eye catching view from 4th floor Window, attached very clean bath (no balcony), clean and daily fresh linen.

17th.. Sr Doctors and physiotherapist started her to walk and bent the new knee to 90°...

This was regular exercise, bending knee to 90° and walking in the corridor with the help of walker and physiotherapist till 19th...

And on 19th all bandage and all drain-pipes ( 3 in total... For Blood to drain our excess blood at operated knee, one for urine, one at spinal joint to push different medicine ) removed and....
discharged in the afternoon by doctor...
Same day, 19th, came to home by evening.

She is recovering nicely.... Walking inside the flat with the help of walker... pain she feel very very rarely.

After 9th day from operation, today (24th March) was the first check up...and it is absolutely OK.
Infact, my wife walk through out the day in hospital alone with the help of walker.
Today, she has been allowed by doctor to move and do morning/evening walk with walker and asked for further check up after 15 days.
No medicine given except multivitamin for further recovery as she has no pain.

We are very very happy for the excellent smooth operation, expertise of doctors, quick recovery process with effective treatment, support of Jr. Doctors, Physiotherapist, Metron, Sisters, Brothers, room boy and aayas for 24×7 and overall management of the hospital.

Well behaved people....
No extra billing...

We, and no one, before surgery, expected that after operation on 2nd day pain would vanish... she would walk and bend knee to 90°and get discharge on 4th day...!!!

All credit goes to Dr. Rahul Bade and his team including Anesthesists Dr. Ganesh Kolhe at Sparsh Multi-Speciality Hospital.

Thank you...well done, doctor !!!
🙏🙏🙏

Thanks to Lt. Col Dr Amogh Yadav from Mumbai and Dr. Rahul Mane for strongly recomanding us the hospital.

(Note : Treatment was going on at Sanchiti Hospital. But operated at Sparsh Multi Speciality Hospital)

The way the hospital handled everything — from lack of transparency, denial of family access, not sharing reports on time, and overall negligence — has left us devastated. What hurts the most is that our child went into the hospital healthy, playing, and eating, and came out only as a body.

Words fall short for the magic I experienced at T Trikon’s Dehne campsite stargazing trip — it was nothing short of soul-stirring!

As soon as we stepped onto the plateau, the sight took my breath away: a row of vibrant orange, blue, green, and red tents glowing like jewels against the towering, flat-topped Sahyadri mountains bathed in molten gold from the setting sun. The sky was on fire — layers of orange, pink, and deep purple melting into each other while the sun slowly sank behind those ancient peaks, painting long shadows across the grassland. I just sat there, speechless, watching nature put on the most dramatic show I’ve ever seen.

Then night fell, and the real wonder began.

The stargazing was pure poetry. Our guide Shreekumar Sir, incredibly passionate and patient, set up this beautiful white telescope “Sanjaya” (named after Sanjay from Mahabharata) and took us on a cosmic journey. He didn’t just point out stars — he brought the sky to life with stories:

- The fierce Greek hunter Orion forever chasing the scorpion across the heavens
- Callisto transformed into the Great Bear (Ursa Major), circling the North Star
- Vain Queen Cassiopeia eternally sitting on her throne in the W-shape
- The inseparable twins Castor & Pollux, one mortal, one divine, bound together in the stars
- Mighty Heracles strangling the Nemean Lion (Leo), its heart marked by the regal star Regulus
- Zeus turning into a majestic white bull to carry away Europa (Taurus), with fiery-eyed Aldebaran glaring from the bull’s face

And then the beautiful Indian parallels — Rohini as the Moon’s beloved, Krittika nurturing Kartikeya, Ashwini Kumaras healing the gods, Sharmistha and Devyani’s tale of rivalry turning to renewal in Punarvasu… And one that moved me deeply: the story of **Saptarishi** and **Krittika**.

The guide pointed to the bright seven stars of the Big Dipper (Saptarishi — the eternal Seven Sages, wise guardians of Vedic knowledge, circling steadfast Dhruva like unchanging dharma). He explained how Agni (the fire god) became infatuated with the beautiful wives of these sages (the Krittikas). When they rejected him out of loyalty, Svaha (Agni’s devoted wife) tricked him by shapeshifting into six of them (except steadfast Arundhati, wife of Vashistha, whose purity made her impossible to imitate).
The six Krittikas ascended to the heavens as the sparkling Pleiades cluster (Krittika Nakshatra), shining eternally as symbols of nurturing fire, purification, and motherhood — while Arundhati remained faithfully beside Vashistha in the Saptarishi group, a beacon of unwavering devotion. Hearing this tale of desire, misunderstanding, sacrifice, and ultimate renewal while gazing at the twinkling Pleiades and the circling Big Dipper felt profoundly moving — like the stars themselves were whispering ancient lessons of balance, loyalty, and transformation right above us!

Around 12:30 am, when the cold started biting and eyelids grew heavy, they brought out steaming hot masala chai — the perfect midnight pick-me-up. Sipping that warm, fragrant tea under a blanket of stars, chatting with fellow stargazers, was one of the coziest, most magical moments of the night.
And the food? Oh my god, the food!
I had requested Jain food in advance and they happily prepared a delicious no-onion-no-garlic version that tasted just as soul-satisfying. Every bite felt like love from a Maharashtrian home kitchen.

The entire setup was spotless, the team warm and super helpful, the vibe relaxed yet full of wonder. Escaping Mumbai’s light pollution to this pristine corner of the Sahyadris, surrounded by mountains, myths, stars— it was everything I didn’t know I needed.

T Trikon didn’t just organize a trip; they created memories that will stay with me forever.
I’m already counting days till my next one — maybe winter for Orion or monsoon for the misty mountains!
Absolute 5 stars. Highly, highly recommended. You owe it to your soul.

– Amrish Sukhadiya
